6:1.sourceText: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὸ Ἀρνίον μίαν ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ σφραγίδων, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγοντος ὡς φωνῇ βροντῆς Ἔρχου.
6:1.targetText: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as it were a voice of thunder, “Come and behold!”

groups.note: Actual hote is ADV in both raw fields, rendered when with the recorded temporal analysis retained.
Actual ēnoixen is aorist active third-singular opening finite, distinct from the seeing/hearing first-person predicates.
Actual henos is genitive-neuter-singular one numeral used substantivally under the hearing construction; the actual genitive remains under English one.
Actual zōōn is genitive-neuter-plural living-creature NOUN, expanded living-creatures without an independent living participle.
Actual legontos is present active genitive-neuter-singular saying participle; its actual case/gender remain, not a source finite or nominative retag.
Actual hōs comparison adverb supplies as-it-were as the English comparison frame. No independently written it pronoun or being verb is printed in this unit.

The exact source form is phōnēi, printed φωνῇ with iota subscript, while BOTH pinned raw fields record N-NSF. Those recorded nominative-feminine-singular analyses are preserved as source annotations without silently retagging the visibly inflected form; complete printed TR instead has phōnēs genitive. English a-voice retains the actual phōnē lexical head.
Actual brontēs is a genitive thunder noun, expanded of-thunder through case without a separate source of preposition.
Actual erchou is present nonactive second-singular coming imperative, not the separate beholding command printed only in TR.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual N1904 explicitly prints the indeclinable seven numeral here, while complete printed TR and the displayed LSV omit seven in the first seals phrase. The real source numeral remains an explained source-only word, not assigned to four in the different creature-count phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: This extra command follows kai/blepe in complete printed TR after Come. Actual N1904 prints only the coming command at this point; no independent conjunction or beholding predicate is invented.

6:2.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων τόξον, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στέφανος, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ.
6:2.targetText: And I saw, and behold, a white horse, and he who is sitting on it is having a bow, and there was given to him a garland, and he went forth overcoming, and that he may overcome.

groups.note: Actual idou has V-2AMM-2S in both raw fields, the second-aorist middle imperative form conventionally rendered behold; the recorded verbal form remains rather than an inferred finite seeing subject.
Actual hippos is anarthrous nominative-masculine-singular horse noun, expanded a ... horse around its independent white adjective.
Actual nominative-masculine-singular article nominalizes the sitting participle and supplies he-who without an independently written personal/relative pronoun.
Actual kathēmenos is present nonactive nominative-masculine-singular sitting PARTICIPLE, rendered finite is-sitting with the real form retained.
Actual auton is ACCUSATIVE-masculine-singular personal pronoun under epi, rendered it for the horse; complete printed TR has dative autō. Its actual accusative remains, not a copied TR case.
Actual echōn is present ACTIVE nominative-masculine-singular having PARTICIPLE, rendered is-having without an independently printed eimi or finite source form.
Actual edothē is AORIST PASSIVE third-singular giving finite, expanded there-was-given as the English presentation frame; no separate there/being source words are printed.
Actual autō is dative-masculine-singular recipient pronoun, expanded to-him through case.
Actual stephanos is the garland/crown noun, rendered a-garland with English indefiniteness, not a source diadēma substituted.
Actual exēlthen is second-aorist active third-singular going-out predicate, expanded he-went-forth with its encoded subject.
Actual nikōn is present active nominative-singular overcoming participle, separate from the following actual aorist subjunctive victory predicate.
Actual nikēsē is AORIST ACTIVE third-singular overcoming SUBJUNCTIVE, expanded he-may-overcome with its encoded subject and modal English realization.

6:3.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν δευτέραν, ἤκουσα τοῦ δευτέρου ζῴου λέγοντος Ἔρχου.
6:3.targetText: And when He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come and behold!”

groups.note: Actual opening finite is aorist active third singular and supplies He-opened through its encoded subject, without an independently printed He pronoun.
Actual genitive-neuter-singular article supplies the determiner in the heard second-living-creature phrase; the actual genitive remains under English the.

Actual coming command is present nonactive second singular; the following TR-only beholding command remains a separate target gap.

unmappedTarget.reason: Complete printed TR adds kai/blepe after the coming command. Actual N1904 has only erchou here; no independent beholding or extra conjunction identity is supplied.

6:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἄλλος ἵππος πυρρός, καὶ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐδόθη αὐτῷ λαβεῖν τὴν εἰρήνην ἐκ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἵνα ἀλλήλους σφάξουσιν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ μάχαιρα μεγάλη.
6:4.targetText: And there went forth another horse—fire-colored, and to him who is sitting on it, there was given to him to take peace from the earth, and that they may slay one another, and there was given to him a great sword.

groups.note: Actual exēlthen is second-aorist active third-singular going-out finite, expanded there-went-forth with the local horse subject, without an independent there word.
Actual pyrros is one nominative-masculine-singular fiery/fire-colored adjective, expanded fire-colored without a separate source fire noun or coloring predicate.

Actual dative-masculine-singular article nominalizes the sitting participle and supplies to-him-who through case and personal nominalization; it is distinct from the following separately printed dative recipient pronoun.
Actual kathēmenō is present nonactive DATIVE-masculine-singular sitting participle, rendered is-sitting without finite-source retag.
Actual auton is accusative-masculine-singular under epi, rendered it for the horse. Complete printed TR has dative autō, not the actual N accusative.
This first actual edothē is aorist passive third-singular giving finite and owns the first there-was-given. The later giving finite keeps its own distinct English occurrence.
This actual autō is the first separately printed dative recipient pronoun in the grant; it owns the second English to-him occurrence after the earlier nominalized article phrase.
Actual ek out-of/source preposition is rendered from; complete printed TR instead has apo. The real ek head remains, not a substituted apo.

Actual sphaxousin is FUTURE ACTIVE third-plural slaying INDICATIVE in BOTH fields, rendered they-may-slay under the purpose frame. Complete printed TR has aorist subjunctive sphaxōsin; the actual future/indicative analysis is retained without an English-driven subjunctive retag.
The second actual edothē is its own aorist passive giving finite, distinct from the preceding grant predicate.

6:5.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τρίτην, ἤκουσα τοῦ τρίτου ζῴου λέγοντος Ἔρχου. καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος μέλας, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων ζυγὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
6:5.targetText: And when He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, “Come and behold!” And I saw, and behold, a black horse, and he who is sitting on it is having a balance in his hand,

Actual auton is accusative-masculine-singular under epi, rendered it for the horse; complete printed TR has dative autō, not a silently substituted actual case.
Actual echōn is present ACTIVE nominative-masculine-singular having participle, rendered is-having without a separate finite being source.
Actual zygon is the accusative-masculine-singular yoke/balance noun, rendered a-balance in this weighing expression; the real zygos head remains, not a weighing verb.

The actual hand article is not separately expressed beside the independently written English his-hand possessor construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: This first English and-behold follows the TR-only kai/blepe after Come. Actual N1904 has only the coming command there. The later real kai/idou pair owns the following and-behold after I-saw, not this added command.

6:6.sourceText: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγουσαν Χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου, καὶ τρεῖς χοίνικες κριθῶν δηναρίου· καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς.
6:6.targetText: and I heard a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying, “A measure of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of barley for a denarius, and you may not injure the oil and the wine.”

groups.note: Actual mesō is a DATIVE-neuter-singular middle adjective used substantivally, expanded the-midst without an independently written article or a source midst-noun retag.
Actual legousan is present active ACCUSATIVE FEMININE singular saying participle, distinct from the genitive creature-related saying forms in the preceding seal announcements.
Actual choinix is an anarthrous nominative-feminine-singular grain-measure noun, rendered A-measure without a separate indefinite article or numeral source.
Actual sitou is genitive-masculine-singular wheat noun, expanded of-wheat through case.
This first actual dēnariou is genitive-neuter-singular price/value noun, expanded for-a-denarius through its price construction, not a printed for preposition.
Actual choinikes is the plural of the preceding grain-measure noun and owns the second measures occurrence, not the first singular measure.

The second actual dēnariou is its own price/value genitive and owns the second for-a-denarius occurrence.

Actual adikēsēs is AORIST ACTIVE second-singular injuring SUBJUNCTIVE under the actual mē negative, rendered you-may ... injure. Its actual prohibitive-subjunctive form remains, not a present indicative or a separately printed you/modal pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual N1904 prints hōs, an as/like comparison before voice. Complete printed TR and displayed LSV omit that comparison word; it is not reassigned to the distinct in-the-midst relation.

6:7.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τετάρτην, ἤκουσα φωνὴν τοῦ τετάρτου ζῴου λέγοντος Ἔρχου.
6:7.targetText: And when He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, “Come and behold!”

groups.note: Actual phōnēn is anarthrous ACCUSATIVE-feminine-singular voice noun, expanded the-voice without an independently printed definite article.

unmappedTarget.reason: Complete printed TR adds kai/blepe after Come; actual N1904 prints no second command or conjunction at this location.

6:8.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος χλωρός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ὁ Θάνατος, καὶ ὁ Ἅιδης ἠκολούθει μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἐξουσία ἐπὶ τὸ τέταρτον τῆς γῆς, ἀποκτεῖναι ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ καὶ ἐν λιμῷ καὶ ἐν θανάτῳ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῆς γῆς.
6:8.targetText: And I saw, and behold, a pale horse, and he who is sitting on him—his name is Death, and Hades follows with him, and there was given to them authority to kill over the fourth part of the earth with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and by the beasts of the earth.

groups.note: Actual chlōros is the nominative-masculine-singular green/pale adjective rendered pale; no source leukos/white adjective is substituted.

Actual autois is dative-masculine-PLURAL recipient pronoun, expanded to-them without substituting a singular recipient or identifying its referents from morphology alone.
Actual tetarton is accusative-neuter-singular FOURTH ordinal adjective used substantivally, expanded fourth-part without an independently printed part noun.
Actual rhomphaia is the dative sword noun here, distinct from the actual machaira noun in6:4; no shared English gloss erases that lexical distinction.
Actual thanatō is the dative death noun and remains a separate occurrence from the earlier nominative Death name; no source disease noun is substituted.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies this copula in the actual name/Death nominal construction. Neither actual N1904 nor complete printed TR writes an independent being verb between name and Death.

6:9.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν πέμπτην σφραγῖδα, εἶδον ὑποκάτω τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν εἶχον.
6:9.targetText: And when He opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those slain because of the word of God, and because of the testimony that they held,

Actual eichon is IMPERFECT ACTIVE third-plural having/holding predicate, rendered they-held with its actual echō head and encoded subject, not an invented independent they pronoun.

6:10.sourceText: καὶ ἔκραξαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες Ἕως πότε, ὁ Δεσπότης ὁ ἅγιος καὶ ἀληθινός, οὐ κρίνεις καὶ ἐκδικεῖς τὸ αἷμα ἡμῶν ἐκ τῶν κατοικούντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
6:10.targetText: and they were crying with a great voice, saying, “Until when, O Master, the Holy and the True, do You not judge and take vengeance of our blood from those dwelling on the earth?”

6:11.targetText: And there was given to each one a white robe, and it was said to them that they may rest themselves yet a short time, until may also be fulfilled their fellow-servants and their brothers, who are about to be killed—even as they.

The actual fellow-servant and brother articles are not separately expressed beside their independently printed English possessors.
